Step 1 [ANCHOR_IDENTIFICATION]: Identify the attachment atom (ANCHOR) and the leaving group (LEAVING).
  Find ANCHOR: The instruction specifies acylating the secondary amine of the piperidine ring. In the indexed SMILES, this is atom 18 (map :18, element N).
  Identify LEAVING: This is an N-acylation (TYPE A addition) where only the hydrogen atom on the amine departs. Therefore, the leaving group is "none".
  FORMAL: INDEXED_SMILES + INSTRUCTION --> ANCHOR(idx=18, element="N") + LEAVING(smiles="none")

Step 2 [FRAGMENT_IDENTIFICATION]: Extract the incoming fragment (ADD_FRAGMENT) and count its heavy atoms.
  The incoming group is a cyanoacetyl group. Its SMILES is "C(=O)CC#N".
  Counting the heavy atoms: 1 carbonyl carbon, 1 carbonyl oxygen, 1 methylene carbon, 1 cyano carbon, and 1 cyano nitrogen. Total = 5 heavy atoms.
  FORMAL: INSTRUCTION --> ADD_FRAGMENT(smiles="C(=O)CC#N", heavy_atoms=5)

Step 3 [PRODUCT_CONSTRUCTION]: Construct the product by bonding ADD_FRAGMENT to ANCHOR.
  TYPE A: Bond the piperidine nitrogen (idx=18) to the carbonyl carbon of the cyanoacetyl group. No heavy atoms are removed.
  FORMAL: SMILES + ANCHOR(idx=18) + LEAVING("none") + ADD_FRAGMENT(smiles="C(=O)CC#N")

Step 4 [HEAVY_ATOM_VERIFICATION]: Verify heavy atom count change.
  The source molecule has 36 heavy atoms (as indicated by the highest atom map number :36).
  The product molecule has 36 + 5 = 41 heavy atoms.
  HEAVY_ATOM_DELTA = 41 - 36 = +5.
  FORMAL: SMILES[n_heavy=36] + PRODUCT_SMILES[n_heavy=41] --> HEAVY_ATOM_DELTA(+5)

Step 5 [RING_VERIFICATION]: Verify ring count change.
  The source molecule contains 5 rings (two phenyl rings, one piperidine ring, and a fused pyrrolo-pyrimidine bicyclic system).
  The product molecule also contains 5 rings.
  RING_DELTA = 5 - 5 = 0.
  FORMAL: SMILES[n_rings=5] + PRODUCT_SMILES[n_rings=5] --> RING_DELTA(0)

  FORMAL: INDEXED_SMILES + INSTRUCTION --> ANCHOR(idx=28, element="O") + LEAVING(smiles="none")

Step 2 [FRAGMENT_IDENTIFICATION]: Extract the incoming fragment (ADD_FRAGMENT) and count its heavy atoms.
  The incoming group is a stearoyl group, which is an 18-carbon acyl chain. Its SMILES is "CCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCC(=O)". It consists of 18 carbon atoms and 1 oxygen atom, giving a total of 19 heavy atoms.
  FORMAL: INSTRUCTION --> ADD_FRAGMENT(smiles="CCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCC(=O)", heavy_atoms=19)

  This is a TYPE A reaction. We bond the hydroxyl oxygen (atom 28) to the carbonyl carbon of the stearoyl group. The resulting product SMILES incorporates the long aliphatic chain attached via an ester linkage.
  FORMAL: SMILES + ANCHOR(idx=28) + LEAVING("none") + ADD_FRAGMENT(smiles="CCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCC(=O)")

Step 4 [HEAVY_ATOM_VERIFICATION]: Verify heavy atom count change.
  The source molecule has 40 heavy atoms (as indicated by the maximum atom map number :40). The product molecule has 59 heavy atoms. The difference is exactly the 19 heavy atoms added from the stearoyl group. HEAVY_ATOM_DELTA = 59 - 40 = +19.
  FORMAL: SMILES[n_heavy=40] + PRODUCT_SMILES[n_heavy=59] --> HEAVY_ATOM_DELTA(+19)

Step 5 [RING_VERIFICATION]: Verify ring count change.
  The source molecule contains 4 rings (three in the fluorenyl-like system and one in the benzyl ester). The product molecule also contains 4 rings, as the stearoyl group is acyclic. RING_DELTA = 4 - 4 = 0.
  FORMAL: SMILES[n_rings=4] + PRODUCT_SMILES[n_rings=4] --> RING_DELTA(0)
